description: A bound written as `500` and the same bound written as `500.0` are one policy, and must hash to one value. This is the case a JavaScript implementation cannot get right by accident: Python's json.loads keeps the int/float distinction the document wrote, and JSON.parse collapses both to one number. An engine that hashes them differently is reproducible only in the language it was written in, which for a hash that approvals and policy pinning are bound to is the same as not being reproducible. Every number reaching the hash is therefore rendered as decimal text first: integral values without a fractional part, the rest in shortest round-trip form.
